messages:
maria: Quick question — can we clarify the intended interface boundary between the eviction manager and prefix ownership/lease layer? Ran into a canary race where an evict path relied on a lease being present and it caused a double-evict scenario.

raj: Short answer: leases were meant to be ownership tokens only, not eviction intent markers. But I know some parts of the eviction code currently read lease state as a proxy for "is owner online" which is confusing.

emily: Yeah that's the crux. Using ownership leases for both liveness and eviction gating conflates responsibilities. We should define two separate primitives (Lease for ownership, EvictIntent for eviction coordination).

ben: Proposal sketch:
- Lease: opaque token, Acquire/Renew/Release semantics, used only to assert owner for reads/writes.
- EvictIntent: explicit action that can be observed and idempotently applied by the owner or other agents.

maria: That helps. How would EvictIntent avoid races when a lease renews at the same time someone sets intent? Example: owner renews -> continues serving, but a delayed EvictIntent arrives and forces eviction mid-flight.

raj: Options:
1) EvictIntent requires owner to acknowledge and release lease (handshake). If owner refuses, eviction aborted.
2) EvictIntent wins if it includes a monotonic epoch greater than lease epoch (preemptive). Owner loses and must gracefully demote.
3) Two-phase: mark intent, wait grace window, then force if no release.

emily: Tradeoffs: (1) is friendly but requires owner cooperation (not reliable under crash). (2) is authoritative but needs careful epoch generation and strong monotonicity across restarts. (3) is pragmatic (dual-phase) but introduces latency and tuning headaches.

ben: I sketched a compact API that we could implement without a big refactor:

```
// Ownership lease
AcquireLease(prefix) -> {lease_id, epoch}
RenewLease(lease_id) -> {ok, epoch}
ReleaseLease(lease_id) -> {ok}

// Eviction intent
MarkEvict(prefix, reason, idempotency_key) -> {intent_id, observed_epoch}
QueryEvict(prefix) -> {intent_id?, observed_epoch?}
ClearEvict(intent_id) -> {ok}
```

The key is that MarkEvict returns observed_epoch so callers can decide whether to escalate.

maria: How do we make MarkEvict idempotent across retries and crash restarts? idempotency_key helps but owner restarts might change epochs.

raj: We store (intent_id, idempotency_key, created_ts, observed_epoch) atomically. If owner restarts and gets a new lease epoch, it compares epochs when deciding whether to accept/clear the intent. If observed_epoch >= lease_epoch -> owner must demote.

emily: We should also instrument the heck out of this: lease_acquire_latency, lease_conflict_count, evict_intent_conflicts, demote_durations, and a small SLI: evict_success_within_window.

ben: Migration plan idea: backward-compatible dual-read. Start writing EvictIntent for new paths while still letting older code use lease-as-proxy. Add a feature flag so we can flip to authoritative mode in canary.

maria: Good. For monotonic epochs we prefer a strictly monotonic counter persisted with leader residency so it survives restarts. UUIDs don't provide ordering. Could we reuse the existing apply-index/term instead of inventing a new store? That might simplify correctness proofs.

raj: Reusing apply-index is attractive but couples this to replication engine; fine if we accept it. Otherwise a small epoch store using RAFT/consensus would work. We need to document failure modes.

emily: Edge case: split-brain during network partition — two nodes think they own lease because they both renewed locally. How does EvictIntent behave? We should make intent resolution authoritative on the control-plane leader (or a sequencer) to avoid divergence.

ben: Agreed. Implementation note: MarkEvict writes intent to control-plane kv that is the single source of truth. Serving nodes watch for updates. That lets us avoid racing state in the local cache.

maria: Ok next steps: Ben, can you spin up a small spike (2-week) that implements the MarkEvict proto + metrics + a canary flip? Include a demo script that shows the three modes (cooperative, epoch-preemptive, delayed-grace)

ben: On it. I'll add a follow-up RFC with API shape and migration steps. Will include example logs and a small sim harness.

raj: +1 on RFC. Also add a quick checklist for potential safety nets: auto fallback to prior model on alarm, and per-tenant opt-outs during rollout.

emily: One more: add a health-check that detects "evict intent churn" and alerts before we flip the flag cluster-wide.

ci-bot: Build #4287 for branch prefix-evict-proto passed.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll open the RFC and tag eng-runtime + eng-sre for rollout gating. :+1:
